:::{#thm-epe-split-noise}
#### The pMSE of a prediction is the pMSE of the mean estimate plus the noise variance

Let:

- $\paren{\newpredvar, \newoutvar}$ be a [new observation](#def-new-observation) relative to the random [training set](#def-training-set) $\trainset$,
- $\noise$ be the [noise](#def-noise) of $\newoutvar$, and
- $\varpar \eqdef \Var{\noise}$ be its [population variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance), which we take to be finite.

Assume $\newpredvar = \predvar$.
Then, given $\newpredvar = \predvar$,
the [expected squared prediction error](#def-epe) (ESPE) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$
is the sum of two terms.
The first is the [irreducible error](#def-irreducible-error) $\varpar$.
The second is the [expected squared estimation error](estimation.qmd#def-mse) (ESEE) of $\predvalf{\predvar}$
as an [estimator](estimation.qmd#def-estimator) of $\truemeanf{\predvar}$:

$$
\ESPE{\predvalf{\predvar}}
= \varpar + \ESEE{\estmeanf{\predvar}}.
$$ {#eq-epe-split-noise}

:::

::: proof
This is @sol-epe-split-noise.
:::
